As anyone may have realized it would be too easy to label any dissenting political movement as a cult. Political cults are not cults because they believe in things that are radical or have tight organization. Although they may arise from radical political sources (and often do). They must share traits with religious cults.

But the issue is unavoidable.

Political cults can become very big, as has been witnessed with the abomination of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia or the more extreme expression of Maoism during the Cultural Revolution the danger for modern cult behaviour is always around the corner.

Here is a (by no means exhaustive) checklist that I have put up that I have collated and based on several online sources:

  • Single conspiratorial group unneeded. Can rely on linked cells or readily identifiable in-group social network.
  • Shared totalitarian ideology/belief system/doctrinal creed (written or in practice), which argues harm done in its name is not wrong. Make it psychologically impossible for members to recognize own fault.
  • Complete loyalty to overall leaders. Absolute commitment to their message. Unquestioning belief in leaders' saviour/teacher/martyr status. Leaders have at stake personal gain and regularly insist on commitments.
  • Dissent, questioning and doubt discouraged, punished and vilified. Shame, guilt, blind faith and ostracism common control techniques.
  • External criticism always portrayed as unjustified assault. External critics are slandered, harassed and undermined on a personal level. Frustrating them to anger is possible motive. Breaking them another. Will create caricature of enemies to ridicule (Five minutes hate e.g.)
  • Polarized us-vs-them mentality. Possible arch-enemy expressed as social group (Jews)/cabal (Illuminati) or combined (e.g. The Patriarchy) Unauthorized engagement with outsiders or opposition demonized.
  • Rationalization of beliefs. Creates arch-narratives that exonerate self/vilify others. Recurved accusations: Will accuse enemy of doing X whilst doing X themselves.
  • Exalted status to members who are blessed, freed, educated etc,. Inculcate entitlement of members that can be controlled.
  • Discriminates based on accidents of birth (race, sex etc,.) or creed as control mechanism, feeding sense of grievance by members. Will whip up hatred, fear of groups and demand asymmetric benefits (whilst insisting such benefits are acceptable).
  • Method of excommunication for violators, who may have penitence allowing rejoining.
  • Claimed access or ownership of special knowledge or human ideals, which makes non-affiliation a sign of personal fault.
  • Scrubbed or sanitized outer message that can be separated from extreme inner doctrines.
  • Will identify self with 'silent majority' when necessary to defend self or equate critics with other extremists to deflect criticism.
  • Cuts ties with family, friends, hides affiliation of cult to them or relationship strained by cult prejudices.
  • May closely identify with sister-ideologies or moderate political movements that fail to recognize the cult's danger and give cult oxygen.
  • Censorship and limiting personal freedom to control information or leave victims psychologically unprepared for cult brutality.
  • Domination of sex lives, sexual mores and bodies to control membership and other.
  • Will subvert media, government and social fabric to impose beliefs externally. Exploits all sympathy. Violence used when effective.
  • Projects faults whilst excusing own (plank in my eye, sawdust in yours).
